items.stem: In C++, when should you prefer composition over inheritance to reuse behaviour?

options.text: When the classes do not form a genuine is-a relationship and you only need to reuse behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: composition avoids a brittle hierarchy when there is no true subtype relationship.

options.text: Always, because inheritance is never useful
options.rationale: Inheritance is appropriate for real is-a relationships.

options.text: Only when performance is the single concern
options.rationale: The choice is primarily about modelling, not raw performance.
Composition is not inherently slow and is often clearer.

items.explanation: Correct: composition avoids a brittle hierarchy when there is no true subtype relationship.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate uses of exceptions in C++? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Signalling that a required file could not be opened
options.rationale: Correct: an unexpected, exceptional condition is a good fit for an exception.

options.text: Reporting that user input failed validation at a boundary
options.rationale: Correct: raising a clear error lets the caller handle invalid input deliberately.

options.text: Controlling normal loop iteration in place of a condition
options.rationale: Using exceptions for ordinary control flow is an anti-pattern.

options.text: Hiding all errors by catching and ignoring them

items.explanation: Correct: an unexpected, exceptional condition is a good fit for an exception.

items.stem: You need fast membership tests on a large, unordered collection of unique keys. Which structure fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: a set gives average constant-time membership tests on unique keys.

options.text: A plain sequential list scanned from the start
options.rationale: Linear scans are slow for membership on large collections.

options.text: A fixed-size array indexed by position
options.rationale: Arrays do not give key-based membership without scanning.

options.text: A single string containing all keys
options.rationale: String search is error-prone and slow for this purpose.

items.explanation: Correct: a set gives average constant-time membership tests on unique keys.
